title: Timeouts retries and cancellation
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of timeouts retries and cancellation
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up

prerequisite.prompt: Recall Approval gates and idempotency. Explain why a recorded result needs its input conditions and evidence source before it can support a claim.
prerequisite.answer: A result depends on the inputs, procedure and conditions that produced it. Preserve data roles and distinguish observed outcomes from predictions or unmeasured conditions. If the prior concept cannot be explained, use a short retrieval activity before this chapter.

vocabulary: The maximum repeat attempts or resources
A request to stop future processing

blocks.text: Timeouts bound waiting; retries consume a finite budget. Cancellation should stop future work while accounting for operations already committed.

Begin by writing the question the procedure is intended to answer. Identify the information already supplied, the information it will produce and the information still missing. These are constructed classroom examples; they do not require live accounts, private records or an external service. Do not treat a plausible explanation as a measured outcome.

Retry only declared transient failures. Use at most three attempts with waiting gaps 1 and 2 seconds; each attempt may run at most 4 seconds. Worst-case elapsed bound excluding overhead is 3*4+1+2=15 seconds.

The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

Change one relevant boundary input, record the outcome and state the contract or statistical assumptions. The program uses fictional values and the Python standard library; it performs no external operations.

lesson.title: Check the boundary and the interpretation

blocks.text: A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur.

A useful check asks what would make the reasoning fail. Distinguish a failure to execute the declared procedure from a weakness in the procedure itself. The first may require a correction; the second requires an explicitly revised method and new evidence. Preserve unsuccessful cases so an improved result cannot hide the original problem.

blocks.label: Guided: restate the worked result, then name the assumption or limitation that prevents a broader conclusion.

lesson.title: Apply the idea and plan the next check

blocks.text: Complete the supported workbook tasks before attempting W4 independently. Record any hints or help used. After feedback, use the teacher's fresh retry rather than copying the earlier answer. For a project, select a relevant new case, predict the outcome from the declared rule and preserve the result alongside any revision.

blocks.label: Exit: propose one revealing change to the worked scenario. State the expected outcome and the evidence that would make you revise your explanation.

workbook.title: Explain the mechanism
workbook.prompt: Explain the weekly mechanism in your own words. Use the worked scenario to name its input, decision rule and output.

workbook.title: Trace the worked case
workbook.prompt: Three attempts each time out after 4 seconds with gaps 1 and 2. A fourth is proposed. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Budget is exhausted after 15 seconds under the model; reject fourth attempt. A late side-effect result must still be reconciled.

workbook.title: Audit the limit
workbook.prompt: A report omits this qualification: A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur. Explain how omitting it could change a reader's interpretation, and write an accurate replacement.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur. State the observed result separately from the unverified or out-of-scope claim; preserve the original evidence rather than inventing a missing fact.

workbook.title: Apply a new case independently
workbook.prompt: Two attempts, each up to 5 seconds, gap 2. Compute bound and decide whether authentication failure should retry.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Bound12 seconds excluding overhead. Authentication failure is non-transient under this policy; do not retry it.

workbook.title: Design a revealing follow-up
workbook.prompt: For the worked scenario, propose one additional case that could reveal a failure, describe its expected outcome before running it, and explain what would need to remain fixed for a fair comparison. Do not reuse W4 as a new final test after receiving feedback.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Accept a concrete variant of the worked input or a missing/conflicting/boundary condition, with an expectation derived from the declared procedure. Require preserved settings, original outputs and data roles. A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur. The new case should test this particular mechanism rather than merely restate the original result.

teacher.background: Two 45-minute sessions. Timeouts bound waiting; retries consume a finite budget. Cancellation should stop future work while accounting for operations already committed. Use the supplied constructed scenarios to make the mechanism inspectable. Collect W4 before sharing solutions. Students should name intermediate evidence and limitations; classroom pacing and learning effectiveness remain unvalidated.

Calculator and optional local Python 3 for arithmetic; no live API or private data

sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite; identify the input, procedure and evidence source.
Explain section 1 and vocabulary. Complete W1 with a mechanism-based explanation.
Trace the declared procedure and worked case. Complete W2, recording intermediate steps.
Discuss the diagram with the worked input; use W3 to distinguish measured claims and limitations.
Retrieve the worked reasoning and collect the guided response before discussing it.
Compare a proposed boundary variant with the original case; identify what remains fixed.
Collect W4 independently. Require the procedure trace and the bounded conclusion.
Use W5 and exit responses for feedback. Administer the fresh retry after feedback and preserve both attempts.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: Budget is exhausted after 15 seconds under the model; reject fourth attempt. A late side-effect result must still be reconciled. Qualification: A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur. Exit: accept a concrete variation with its predicted outcome and a stated condition that would challenge the mechanism; reject a claim resting on unmeasured evidence.
misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A timeout means the caller lacks a timely result, not necessarily that the remote operation did not occur.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
teacher.assessment: W4: Bound12 seconds excluding overhead. Authentication failure is non-transient under this policy; do not retry it. Require intermediate reasoning and the stated scope. Fresh retry: Four attempts, each up to 2 seconds, gaps1, 2, 4. Expected reasoning: Bound15 seconds. Cancellation prevents new attempts; it cannot undo an already committed effect. If students need support, record it and reassess with another new case rather than awarding independence to a copied answer.
teacher.support: Provide an input/procedure/result/limit frame and a calculator when needed. Ask students to identify the first step before completing the whole trace. Extension: compare two concrete variants of this mechanism while holding unrelated conditions fixed; report both successful and unsuccessful outcomes.
